# Lab 15.5: Use Case: Fraud Detection

## What We Are Going to Do
Use graph patterns to find money that goes round in a circle, and accounts linked to a blocked account.

## Steps

1. **[SQL] Find transfer cycles.** Money that leaves an account and comes back in 2–4 hops is a classic laundering pattern:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">GRAPH lab15.FinGraph
MATCH p = (a:Account)-[t:Transfers]-&gt;{2,4}(b:Account)
WHERE a.id = b.id
RETURN a.id AS account, ARRAY_LENGTH(t) AS hops;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Accounts 7 → 16 → 20 → 7 form a loop.

2. **[SQL] People within 2 hops of a blocked account.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">GRAPH lab15.FinGraph
MATCH (blocked:Account {is_blocked: TRUE})&lt;-[:Transfers]-{1,2}(a:Account)&lt;-[:Owns]-(p:Person)
RETURN DISTINCT p.name, p.city;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **[SQL] Save the risk list as a table.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE lab15.risky_people AS
SELECT DISTINCT name, city
FROM GRAPH_TABLE(lab15.FinGraph
  MATCH (blocked:Account {is_blocked: TRUE})&lt;-[:Transfers]-{1,2}(a:Account)&lt;-[:Owns]-(p:Person)
  COLUMNS (p.name AS name, p.city AS city));</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **[Console] Visualise the loop.** In a notebook, run step 1 with `RETURN TO_JSON(p) AS path` and `%%bigquery --graph`.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Cycle | 7 → 16 → 20 → 7 |
| Blocked-account links | People who sent money towards account 16 |
| Output | `lab15.risky_people` table |
| Why graph | Multi-hop questions are short in GQL, long in SQL |
